audit.why: 52.16% over 717 games. The purest version of the Pantheon lane — you win every level until he has stacks, then you lose everything. Both layers already say so and the mirror at audits/top/nasus__pantheon.json agrees from his side.
Spikes are placed right: your levels 1-2 before Wither, your level 3 kill window, your first item as the last clean one, and his two-item stacked-Q timing.

audit.whatIsWrong: late says his shred 'ignores your shields' and 'your shields mean nothing', and whys[6] repeats it. There are no shields, plural, in Pantheon's kit — there is one, Aegis Assault, and it is not what loses this fight.
audit.why: The mirror audit found the root of this on his side: the dataset carries a stale claim that Pantheon's passive blocks attacks, which was Aegis Protection before the rework and is now Mortal Will, an empowerment on his next spell. The plural 'shields' on my page is the same fossil pointing the player at defences he does not have. What actually loses the late fight is specific and worth saying: Fury of the Sands deals percent-max-health magic damage, so armour is the wrong purchase against it, and Spirit Fire reduces the armour you did buy.
audit.corrected: The shields language replaced with the real mechanics — percent-health magic damage from Fury of the Sands and armour reduction from Spirit Fire.

audit.whatIsWrong: Packet flags zero sequencing cues, and Wither — the ability the page tells you to fear four times — has no number on it.
audit.why: Wither is 15/14/13/12/11s and 700 range, which outranges Shield Vault's 600. That means he can start it before you can answer, and it also means the fifteen seconds after he uses it is the only clean all-in window you get. Siphoning Strike falls from 7.5s to 3.5s, so denying stacks gets harder every rank. Spirit Fire is a flat 12s and Fury of the Sands 120s at rank 1. The mirror confirms the important negative: Nasus has no hard CC at all, so nothing he owns interrupts your Aegis Assault — Wither is a slow, and slows do not cancel channels.
audit.corrected: Wither's 15s and 700 range written into early and mid, with the all-in keyed to it.

Tip the spear at him every time he steps up for a minion so his Siphoning Strike stacks crawl — a denied Nasus is a dead Nasus. At 6, Grand Starfall is your tool: he can't roam or contest objectives like you can, so leap to other lanes and snowball the map while he's stuck farming. Keep pushing your accumulated tempo into kills and dives before your damage plateaus.

notes: MIRROR REUSE: audits/top/nasus__pantheon.json found that the dataset carries a stale claim that Pantheon's passive blocks basic attacks — that was Aegis Protection, removed in his rework, and Mortal Will only empowers his next spell. My side of this matchup carries the same fossil in a different form: late and whys[6] both talk about 'your shields', plural, meaning nothing against him. Pantheon has one defensive cooldown, Aegis Assault, and it is not what loses this fight. Replaced with the two mechanics that do: Fury of the Sands deals percent-max-health magic damage, which armour does not reduce, and Spirit Fire strips armour outright. The mirror's other useful negative is honoured here — Nasus has no hard CC anywhere in his kit, Wither is a slow, and slows do not cancel channels, so nothing he owns interrupts Aegis Assault. I have said that explicitly rather than leaving it implied. Best new number: Wither is 700 range against Shield Vault's 600, so he opens every trade from outside your engage, and its 15s cooldown at rank 1 is the only window where you can stay on him.
